messages.content: Explain how an airplane wing generates lift. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: An airplane wing generates lift primarily through its shape, called an airfoil, which is curved on top and flatter on the bottom. As air flows over the wing, it moves faster over the curved top surface, creating lower pressure above the wing compared to the higher pressure below. This pressure difference produces an upward force—lift—that keeps the plane airborne. The angle of the wing (angle of attack) also affects lift by directing more air downward, increasing the pressure difference.
